answers.reasoning: Differentiate x and y with respect to theta1 and theta2. First column contains both link contributions, second only the second link. dx derivatives have negative sine signs; dy derivatives have positive cosine signs. This is o1.

At theta1=30°,theta2=60°, J=[[-3/2,-1],[sqrt(3)/2,0]]. The y equation gives q1dot=4/sqrt(3). Then the x equation gives q2dot=-1-(3/2)(4/sqrt(3))=-1-2sqrt(3). Direct substitution reproduces both commanded components(1,2).
The translational contribution is2*0.5+(-1)*2+3*(-1)=-4 W. The rotational contribution is1*2+4*(-0.5)+(-2)*1=-2 W. The common-origin, common-basis total is -6 W, not either component alone.
